---
title: Missing values
description: How polars-umap treats nulls, NaN and infinite values.
jupyter: python3
---

A row is **invalid** when it is null, or contains a null, NaN or infinite value. UMAP can't place
such a row, so polars-umap gives you two options through `null_policy`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl

import polars_umap as pu

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
rows = rng.normal(size=(50, 3)).tolist()
rows[3] = None
rows[10] = [1.0, None, 2.0]
rows[20] = [1.0, float("nan"), 2.0]
df = pl.DataFrame({"embedding": rows}, schema={"embedding": pl.Array(pl.Float64, 3)})
```

```{python}
df.filter(pl.int_range(pl.len()).is_in([3, 10, 20]))
```

## `null_policy="error"` (default)

Invalid rows raise an error that says how many there are and where the first one is:

```{python}
#| error: true
df.select(pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform())
```

## `null_policy="ignore"`

UMAP is fitted on the valid rows only, and the invalid rows get a null result. The output still
has one row per input row, so it lines up with the rest of the frame:

```{python}
out = df.with_columns(
    xy=pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform(null_policy="ignore", random_state=0)
)
out.filter(pl.col("xy").is_null())
```

The valid rows get exactly the embedding they would get if the invalid rows weren't there.

## Nearest neighbors

`knn()` supports the same policy. Ignored rows get a null result, and they never appear as
someone else's neighbor:

```{python}
df.select(pl.col("embedding").umap.knn(k=3, null_policy="ignore")).head(5)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Zero vectors and cosine distance

An all-zero vector has no direction, so its cosine distance to anything is undefined. Text
embeddings of empty documents are a common source of them. Turn them into nulls first:

```python
df.with_columns(
    pl.when(
        pl.col("embedding").arr.to_list().list.eval(pl.element().abs()).list.sum() > 0
    ).then(pl.col("embedding"))
)
```
:::
